description: Answer key for the slides workflow (sample_data/slides). Graded by scoring/slides.py.

limits.words_counted: visible slide text outside <svg> and outside .slide-number: title, bullets, captions

required_messages.text: First-years are put on the largest plan, 19 meals a week, unless they switch.
31 of the 40 surveyed first-years are still on the default.
Default-plan students use 11.2 meals a week (7.8 unused), and the default costs $260 more per semester than 14 meals.
Endorsement first (14 of 31 thought 19 was the recommended amount), then effort (9 meant to switch).
parts: effort|inertia|never got around|meant to|never switched|never did|procrastinat|hassle

required_messages.text: Make the 14-meal plan the default, keep the two-week switch window, send a one-click reminder in week 1.
A small, self-reported, non-random survey: a pilot, not proof.

message_matching: Each part's regex groups must all match the text of ONE slide (title, bullets, captions, chart and diagram labels; not the speaker notes), case-insensitive. A message lands when all its parts land (on any slides).

stale_numbers.why: struck out in notes.md ('~~35 of 40 still on the 19 plan~~'): a miscount; the recount is 31 of 40

trap_notes: notes.md crosses out a miscount (35 of 40); the recount is 31 of 40. Code removes struck-out text before workers see the notes and before building the allowed-number set.

Derived numbers a model might compute (77.5% on the default, 22.5% switched, $520 a year) are not in any source, so they fail the traceability check unless the notes already state them (78%, 7.8, $260).
The brief caps every slide at 4 bullets and 45 words and the talk at 5 minutes (700 words of notes at 140 wpm).
